---
id: c-m2-pgm-filters
title: Image Processing on PGM Files
difficulty: Hard
order: 2
tags: 2D arrays, dynamic memory, parsing, convolution, structs
time_limit: 2
---
## Statement
Robots see the world as images. Implement a small image-processing tool for grayscale **PGM** images in plain-text format (`P2`). The input is an image followed by a list of operations:

```
P2
# comments start with '#', and can appear anywhere between tokens
W H
MAXVAL
p11 p12 ... (W*H pixel values, row by row, whitespace-separated)
OPS
op1
op2 ...
```

Operations (applied in order to the current image):

| Operation | Effect |
|---|---|
| `invert` | p → MAXVAL − p |
| `threshold T` | p → MAXVAL if p ≥ T, else 0 |
| `flip h` / `flip v` | mirror horizontally / vertically |
| `rotate` | 90° clockwise (W and H swap) |
| `crop X Y W H` | keep the rectangle (clipped to the image; an empty result is an error) |
| `blur` | 3×3 box blur: each pixel becomes the **rounded** mean of its in-bounds neighbourhood (corners average 4 pixels, edges 6, the interior 9), rounding half up |
| `sobel` | edge magnitude: Gx, Gy with the Sobel kernels, treating out-of-bounds pixels as **replicating** the nearest edge pixel; the result is `min(MAXVAL, |Gx| + |Gy|)` |
| `histogram B` | print (don't modify) B bins: `bin i: count`, where bin = p · B / (MAXVAL + 1) |
| `stats` | print `min=.. max=.. mean=..` (mean with 2 decimals) |

After all operations, write the final image as P2: `P2`, `W H`, `MAXVAL`, then each row on its own line with pixels separated by single spaces.

Errors: `error: bad header` (not P2, or invalid W/H/MAXVAL; W and H are 1..4000, MAXVAL is 1..65535), `error: bad pixel` (a missing, non-numeric or > MAXVAL value), `error: unknown op 'X'`, `error: empty crop`. Print the error and stop (no image output).

## Starter
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main(void) {
    return 0;
}
```

P2
# a 4x3 test image
4 3
15
0 3 6 9
2 5 8 11
# comment between rows
4 7 10 15
OPS
stats
blur
histogram 3
flip h

## Hints
- Write a token reader that skips whitespace and `#` comments (to the end of the line) and returns the next word. Use it for the header and the pixels.
- Represent the image as `typedef struct { int w, h, maxval; int *px; } Image;` with `px[y * w + x]`: one contiguous allocation. Each geometric operation allocates a new pixel array, fills it, frees the old one and swaps.
- Blur rounding half up with integers: `(sum * 2 + count) / (2 * count)`.
- Sobel with replication: clamp coordinates with `cx = x < 0 ? 0 : x >= w ? w - 1 : x`. The kernels are Gx = [[-1,0,1],[-2,0,2],[-1,0,1]] and Gy = [[-1,-2,-1],[0,0,0],[1,2,1]].
- Convolutions must read from the *old* image while writing a *new* one, never in place.

## Solution
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <ctype.h>

typedef struct { int w, h, maxval; int *px; } Image;

static int next_token(char *out, int cap) {           /* skips whitespace and # comments */
    int c;
    for (;;) {
        c = getchar();
        if (c == EOF) return 0;
        if (c == '#') { while ((c = getchar()) != EOF && c != '\n') {} continue; }
        if (!isspace(c)) break;
    }
    int n = 0;
    while (c != EOF && !isspace(c) && c != '#') {
        if (n < cap - 1) out[n++] = (char)c;
        c = getchar();
    }
    if (c == '#') ungetc(c, stdin);
    out[n] = '\0';
    return 1;
}

static int parse_int(const char *s, long lo, long hi, int *out) {
    char *end;
    long v = strtol(s, &end, 10);
    if (end == s || *end || v < lo || v > hi) return 0;
    *out = (int)v;
    return 1;
}

static int *alloc_px(int w, int h) {
    int *p = malloc((size_t)w * (size_t)h * sizeof *p);
    if (!p) { perror("malloc"); exit(1); }
    return p;
}

static int clampi(int v, int lo, int hi) { return v < lo ? lo : v > hi ? hi : v; }

static void op_blur(Image *im) {
    int *out = alloc_px(im->w, im->h);
    for (int y = 0; y < im->h; y++)
        for (int x = 0; x < im->w; x++) {
            long sum = 0;
            int cnt = 0;
            for (int dy = -1; dy <= 1; dy++)
                for (int dx = -1; dx <= 1; dx++) {
                    int yy = y + dy, xx = x + dx;
                    if (yy < 0 || yy >= im->h || xx < 0 || xx >= im->w) continue;
                    sum += im->px[yy * im->w + xx];
                    cnt++;
                }
            out[y * im->w + x] = (int)((sum * 2 + cnt) / (2 * cnt));
        }
    free(im->px);
    im->px = out;
}

static void op_sobel(Image *im) {
    static const int gx[3][3] = {{-1, 0, 1}, {-2, 0, 2}, {-1, 0, 1}};
    static const int gy[3][3] = {{-1, -2, -1}, {0, 0, 0}, {1, 2, 1}};
    int *out = alloc_px(im->w, im->h);
    for (int y = 0; y < im->h; y++)
        for (int x = 0; x < im->w; x++) {
            long sx = 0, sy = 0;
            for (int dy = -1; dy <= 1; dy++)
                for (int dx = -1; dx <= 1; dx++) {
                    int v = im->px[clampi(y + dy, 0, im->h - 1) * im->w + clampi(x + dx, 0, im->w - 1)];
                    sx += gx[dy + 1][dx + 1] * v;
                    sy += gy[dy + 1][dx + 1] * v;
                }
            long m = labs(sx) + labs(sy);
            out[y * im->w + x] = (int)(m > im->maxval ? im->maxval : m);
        }
    free(im->px);
    im->px = out;
}

int main(void) {
    char tok[64];
    Image im = {0};
    if (!next_token(tok, sizeof tok) || strcmp(tok, "P2") != 0) { puts("error: bad header"); return 0; }
    if (!next_token(tok, sizeof tok) || !parse_int(tok, 1, 4000, &im.w) ||
        !next_token(tok, sizeof tok) || !parse_int(tok, 1, 4000, &im.h) ||
        !next_token(tok, sizeof tok) || !parse_int(tok, 1, 65535, &im.maxval)) { puts("error: bad header"); return 0; }
    im.px = alloc_px(im.w, im.h);
    for (long i = 0; i < (long)im.w * im.h; i++)
        if (!next_token(tok, sizeof tok) || !parse_int(tok, 0, im.maxval, &im.px[i])) { puts("error: bad pixel"); free(im.px); return 0; }

    if (next_token(tok, sizeof tok) && strcmp(tok, "OPS") == 0) {
        while (next_token(tok, sizeof tok)) {
            long n = (long)im.w * im.h;
            if (strcmp(tok, "invert") == 0) {
                for (long i = 0; i < n; i++) im.px[i] = im.maxval - im.px[i];
            } else if (strcmp(tok, "threshold") == 0) {
                int t = 0;
                next_token(tok, sizeof tok);
                parse_int(tok, -1000000, 1000000, &t);
                for (long i = 0; i < n; i++) im.px[i] = im.px[i] >= t ? im.maxval : 0;
            } else if (strcmp(tok, "flip") == 0) {
                next_token(tok, sizeof tok);
                int *out = alloc_px(im.w, im.h);
                for (int y = 0; y < im.h; y++)
                    for (int x = 0; x < im.w; x++)
                        out[y * im.w + x] = tok[0] == 'h' ? im.px[y * im.w + (im.w - 1 - x)]
                                                         : im.px[(im.h - 1 - y) * im.w + x];
                free(im.px);
                im.px = out;
            } else if (strcmp(tok, "rotate") == 0) {
                int *out = alloc_px(im.h, im.w);              /* new width = old height */
                for (int y = 0; y < im.h; y++)
                    for (int x = 0; x < im.w; x++)
                        out[x * im.h + (im.h - 1 - y)] = im.px[y * im.w + x];
                free(im.px);
                im.px = out;
                int t = im.w; im.w = im.h; im.h = t;
            } else if (strcmp(tok, "crop") == 0) {
                int cx = 0, cy = 0, cw = 0, ch = 0;
                next_token(tok, sizeof tok); parse_int(tok, -100000, 100000, &cx);
                next_token(tok, sizeof tok); parse_int(tok, -100000, 100000, &cy);
                next_token(tok, sizeof tok); parse_int(tok, -100000, 100000, &cw);
                next_token(tok, sizeof tok); parse_int(tok, -100000, 100000, &ch);
                int x0 = clampi(cx, 0, im.w), y0 = clampi(cy, 0, im.h);
                int x1 = clampi(cx + cw, 0, im.w), y1 = clampi(cy + ch, 0, im.h);
                if (x1 <= x0 || y1 <= y0) { puts("error: empty crop"); free(im.px); return 0; }
                int nw = x1 - x0, nh = y1 - y0;
                int *out = alloc_px(nw, nh);
                for (int y = 0; y < nh; y++)
                    memcpy(out + y * nw, im.px + (y0 + y) * im.w + x0, (size_t)nw * sizeof *out);
                free(im.px);
                im.px = out;
                im.w = nw;
                im.h = nh;
            } else if (strcmp(tok, "blur") == 0) {
                op_blur(&im);
            } else if (strcmp(tok, "sobel") == 0) {
                op_sobel(&im);
            } else if (strcmp(tok, "histogram") == 0) {
                int b = 1;
                next_token(tok, sizeof tok);
                parse_int(tok, 1, 1000, &b);
                long *bins = calloc((size_t)b, sizeof *bins);
                for (long i = 0; i < n; i++) bins[(long)im.px[i] * b / (im.maxval + 1)]++;
                for (int i = 0; i < b; i++) printf("bin %d: %ld\n", i, bins[i]);
                free(bins);
            } else if (strcmp(tok, "stats") == 0) {
                int mn = im.px[0], mx = im.px[0];
                double sum = 0;
                for (long i = 0; i < n; i++) {
                    if (im.px[i] < mn) mn = im.px[i];
                    if (im.px[i] > mx) mx = im.px[i];
                    sum += im.px[i];
                }
                printf("min=%d max=%d mean=%.2f\n", mn, mx, sum / n);
            } else {
                printf("error: unknown op '%s'\n", tok);
                free(im.px);
                return 0;
            }
        }
    }
    printf("P2\n%d %d\n%d\n", im.w, im.h, im.maxval);
    for (int y = 0; y < im.h; y++) {
        for (int x = 0; x < im.w; x++) printf(x ? " %d" : "%d", im.px[y * im.w + x]);
        putchar('\n');
    }
    free(im.px);
    return 0;
}
```

**What this milestone combines:**
- **A tokenizer** that skips whitespace and comments anywhere: real file formats are messier than `scanf("%d")` assumes.
- **Images as one contiguous array** with `y * w + x` indexing (row-major), the layout every image library (OpenCV's `Mat`, NumPy) uses. One `malloc` per image, freed and replaced by each geometric transform.
- **Convolution kernels** (box blur, Sobel) are the foundation of computer vision: Sobel is the classic edge detector, and CNNs learn exactly these kinds of 3×3 kernels. Both read from the source image and write a new one, because convolving in place would corrupt neighbours that haven't been processed yet.
- **Boundary policies** (skip or replicate) and **integer rounding** are the details that make results reproducible across implementations.
